issues.t: Clutch pedal sticks to the floor
issues.sym: After hard or hot driving the clutch pedal goes soft, stays down on the floor, and you cannot shift gears. Once the car cools the pedal often comes back.
issues.why: From 2007 Nissan used a clutch slave cylinder that sits inside the bell housing. Owners and a class action lawsuit say heat from the transmission can boil the clutch fluid, creating air in the system so the pedal loses pressure. Manual 370Zs were the subject of lawsuits over the same symptom.
issues.next: If the pedal sticks, pull over safely and let the car cool. Have the clutch fluid bled and the slave cylinder checked. Many owners fit an updated slave cylinder or an external slave conversion when the clutch is replaced.

issues.t: Manual gearbox grinds going into gear
issues.sym: Grinding or crunching when shifting, most often into 3rd, 5th or 6th, or from 1st to 2nd on a cold gearbox. Some cars pop out of gear under load.
issues.why: The synchronizer rings inside the 6-speed manual wear out, especially with hard driving. Owners of both the 350Z and 370Z report synchro wear and gearbox replacements.
issues.next: Try fresh gear oil of the correct type first, which can help a little. If grinding continues, have a transmission shop inspect the synchros before more gears are damaged.

issues.t: Excessive oil consumption on 2005-2006 manual cars
issues.sym: The oil level drops quickly between changes, the low oil light may come on, and some engines make an unusual noise.
issues.why: The higher-revving engine used in 2005 Track and anniversary models and 2006 manual cars can burn oil. Nissan published a bulletin with an oil consumption test and replaced the short block on engines that failed it.
issues.next: Check the dipstick every fill-up and top up as needed. Running low can damage the timing chain and bearings. Ask a Nissan dealer to perform the oil consumption test.

issues.t: Oil gallery gasket failure
issues.sym: Check engine light with codes P0011 or P0021, a sudden drop in oil pressure, limp mode, or oil seeping near the back of the engine.
issues.why: Small gaskets that seal oil passages behind the timing cover can harden and leak, so the variable valve timing loses oil pressure. Nissan revised the gasket design around 2012.
issues.next: Do not keep driving if the oil pressure light comes on. Have a shop confirm the codes and replace the gaskets with the updated design. Changing them before they fail can prevent engine damage.

issues.t: Crank or cam sensor can stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: The service engine soon light comes on, the engine loses power, stalls while driving, or will not start.
issues.why: A faulty weld in the crankshaft or camshaft position sensors on early cars could make them fail.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Confirm the recall was done. If it was and the engine still stalls, have the sensors tested again.

issues.t: Camshaft position sensor failure
issues.sym: Stalling, hard starting, a rough idle or a check engine light, often when the engine is warm.
issues.why: Camshaft position sensors keep failing on these engines even outside the 2003 recall. They are among the most reported repairs in owner surveys.
issues.next: Have the codes read. Replacing the camshaft sensors (and the crank sensor if it is also flagged) is usually a quick job.

issues.t: Fuel filler hose can crack and leak (recall)
issues.sym: A gasoline smell near the rear of the car or fuel dripping after you fill up.
issues.why: The rubber hose between the filler neck and the tank can crack and leak fuel, creating a fire risk.
issues.next: If you smell fuel, do not park in a closed garage and get it checked. Confirm the free recall hose replacement was done.

issues.t: Timing chain rattle on cold start
issues.sym: A rattle or whine from the front of the engine for a few seconds after a cold start, sometimes with a check engine light.
issues.why: The timing chain guides and tensioner wear with age and mileage, and low or old oil speeds this up, letting the chain slap.
issues.next: Keep the oil topped up and changed on time. If the rattle lasts longer or gets louder, have the chain guides inspected before the chain jumps a tooth.

issues.t: Ticking or knocking at idle from the fuel line
issues.sym: A ticking or knocking sound you can hear in the cabin when the engine idles.
issues.why: Pressure pulses in the fuel line cause the noise. Nissan released a revised fuel damper and hose to quiet it.
issues.next: This is not harmful, but a dealer or shop can install the revised damper if the noise bothers you.

issues.t: Power window stops working or won't close fully
issues.sym: A window that moves slowly, stops partway, will not go up, or loses its auto up and down. These frameless windows also drop slightly when the door opens, so a failing window can stop the door from closing properly.
issues.why: Window motors and regulators are the most reported repair in TrueDelta's owner survey for this car. The windows can also lose their settings after the battery is disconnected and need re-learning.
issues.next: Try the window reset procedure in the owner's manual first. If it still fails, have the motor and regulator checked. Keep the car covered if a window will not close.

issues.t: Worn front compression rod bushings
issues.sym: Clunking over bumps, a shimmy or vibration under braking, vague steering, or uneven front tire wear.
issues.why: The large rubber bushings on the front compression rods wear out and crack over time. Left too long, the whole arm may need replacing.
issues.next: Have the front suspension inspected. Replacing the bushings early, often with firmer aftermarket ones, is a smaller job than replacing arms.

issues.t: Tires wear out quickly on the inner edges
issues.sym: Tires, especially the rear or front inside edges, wear down far faster than expected, sometimes needing replacement in under a year.
issues.why: The factory alignment settings and worn suspension parts on these cars put a lot of camber on the tires, which wears the inside edges. Tire wear is one of the biggest complaint areas for early 350Zs.
issues.next: Check tire edges regularly. A careful alignment closer to zero toe, plus replacing worn bushings, helps tires last much longer.

issues.t: Clicking from the rear axles when pulling away
issues.sym: A click or clunk from one or both rear wheels when you accelerate from a stop.
issues.why: Nissan traced it to the joint between the rear driveshaft and the wheel hub. Its bulletin calls for cleaning the flange surface and adding a special grease.
issues.next: Ask a dealer or shop to perform the bulletin repair. If clicking continues, have the outer CV joints checked for wear.

issues.t: Passenger airbag may be switched off by mistake (recall)
issues.sym: The passenger airbag off light may stay lit even with an adult in the seat.
issues.why: A part in the passenger seat occupant sensor could be out of spec and interrupt its signal, so the system turns the passenger airbag off.
issues.next: Confirm the recall was done. The dealer tests the system and replaces the sensor if needed under the recall.

issues.t: Steering lock fails and the car won't start
issues.sym: The push-button start does nothing or shows a steering lock warning, and the steering wheel stays locked. The car cannot be driven.
issues.why: Oil can get inside the electronic steering column lock unit, so the body computer will not allow the engine to start. Nissan ran a free service campaign to replace the unit on many 2009-2010 370Zs.
issues.next: Ask a Nissan dealer whether campaign P3208 applies to your car. If not, the lock unit can be replaced, and some shops offer other repair options.

issues.t: Power window may not reverse when it hits something (recall)
issues.sym: The auto-up window keeps pushing when it meets an obstruction instead of backing down, which can pinch fingers.
issues.why: A programming error in some window switches required too much force before the auto-reverse kicked in.
issues.next: Use care with the auto-up window and get the free switch replacement done.

issues.t: Driver curtain airbag may be installed wrong (recall)
issues.sym: No visible signs. The airbag may not deploy correctly in a side crash.
issues.why: A small number of 2018 370Zs may have had the driver-side curtain airbag installed incorrectly at the factory.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the open recall. The dealer inspects and corrects the airbag for free.

issues.t: Clogged or rattling catalytic converters
issues.sym: A rattle from under the car, misfires, a check engine light, rough idle or a loss of power.
issues.why: If the engine runs hot or misfires, the honeycomb inside the converters can melt or break apart, which blocks the exhaust. It has been seen from about 75,000 miles.
issues.next: Fix any misfire right away to protect the converters. If a converter is rattling or clogged, have the exhaust back-pressure tested before replacing parts.

issues.t: Water pump leaks or fails
issues.sym: Coolant leaking from the front of the engine, a whining noise, or the temperature gauge climbing.
issues.why: The water pump wears out with mileage, usually around 100,000 miles.
issues.next: If the engine starts to overheat, stop and let it cool. Replace the pump at the first sign of a leak, and consider the thermostat at the same time.

issues.t: Rear hatch won't pop up or stay open
issues.sym: The hatch unlatches but does not lift, or slowly drops back down when opened.
issues.why: The gas struts that hold the hatch up lose pressure with age. This is the most common 370Z problem on RepairPal.
issues.next: Replace both hatch struts. It is an easy job, and a falling hatch can hurt someone.

issues.t: Soft clutch pedal from a leaking master cylinder
issues.sym: The clutch pedal feels soft or spongy, sinks, or the clutch does not fully release, making shifts hard.
issues.why: The clutch master cylinder and slave cylinder seals can leak internally. Owner surveys list both cylinders among the top repairs for these cars.
issues.next: Check the clutch fluid level (it shares the brake reservoir on many cars). Have the hydraulic parts inspected and the fluid bled.

issues.t: A/C compressor or condenser failure
issues.sym: The A/C blows warm air or makes noise when it switches on.
issues.why: Owners report failed A/C compressors and condensers on these cars. The condenser sits low in the front and can be damaged by road debris.
issues.next: Have the system checked for leaks and pressure. If the compressor failed, the system should be flushed when the new one goes in.

issues.t: Convertible top tears or top motor fails
issues.sym: The soft top on Roadster models tears or wears through, leaks, or the power top stops moving.
issues.why: Owners report worn and torn fabric tops and failed top motors on Roadsters as they age.
issues.next: Keep the top clean and treated. Have a leaking or stuck top looked at by a convertible top specialist rather than forcing it.

issues.t: Rear differential whine or clunk
issues.sym: A whine when you lift off the throttle, or a clunk from the rear when getting on and off the gas.
issues.why: The ring and pinion gears in the differential can wear, and the differential mount bushings soften over time.
issues.next: Change the differential fluid and check its color. Dark fluid or a loud whine means the differential should be inspected.

issues.t: Car may roll away in Park (recall)
issues.sym: The car could roll even with the 9-speed automatic shifter in Park.
issues.why: The parking pawl inside the automatic may not fully engage because of extra resistance in the park mechanism.
issues.next: Always set the parking brake until the free transmission computer update is done.

issues.t: Pop-up hood may not lift in a crash (recall)
issues.sym: No visible signs. The hood may not raise to cushion a pedestrian in a frontal crash.
issues.why: Fasteners on the left front bumper reinforcement clip can loosen and keep the pop-up hood system from working.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer tightens the fasteners for free.

issues.t: Pedestrian sensor wiring may be reversed (recall)
issues.sym: Usually none, though a warning for the pop-up hood system may appear. The hood may not lift in a pedestrian crash.
issues.why: Connectors for the right-side pedestrian sensors may have been swapped in the front bumper wiring harness.
issues.next: Get the free bumper harness replacement done. Check your VIN for open recalls.

issues.t: Notchy shifting or grinding in the 6-speed manual
issues.sym: Shifts feel notchy, especially 1st to 2nd, and some cars grind going into gear.
issues.why: The cause is not confirmed. Owners suspect the stronger gearbox parts needed for the twin-turbo engine. Nissan also issued dealer actions on early cars to inspect a 5th-gear shift lever plate.
issues.next: Let the car warm up before shifting hard, and report grinding to a Nissan dealer while the car is under warranty.

issues.t: Check engine light with mass airflow codes
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with codes P0101 or P010B. The car may drive normally.
issues.why: Nissan issued a bulletin for these mass airflow sensor circuit codes on the 2023 Z.
issues.next: Have the codes read and ask a Nissan dealer about the related bulletin. It is often covered by the new car warranty.

issues.t: Key not detected and engine won't start
issues.sym: A key not detected message appears and the push-button start will not start the engine.
issues.why: Nissan's bulletin covers the intelligent key not being recognized. A weak key fob battery or interference can also cause it.
issues.next: Hold the key fob against the start button and press it; this usually starts the car. Replace the fob battery, and ask the dealer about the bulletin if it keeps happening.
